articles.title: Drawing a believable iMessage screenshot on a canvas
articles.excerpt: I built a fake text message editor that runs in the browser, and most of the work went into small details that make a screenshot read as a real phone. The preview is drawn on a canvas, not built from…
articles.body: I built a fake text message editor that runs in the browser, and most of the work went into small details that make a screenshot read as a real phone. The preview is drawn on a canvas, not built from DOM elements. That keeps the PNG export identical to what you see: the same drawing code renders the preview and the 1206 × 2622 export, which is the pixel size of a recent iPhone screen. A few things that mattered more than I expected: Bubble tails only go on the last message in a run from the same person. Put a tail on every bubble and it looks wrong straight away. "Delivered" and "Read 9:41 PM" sit under the last sent message only, in small grey text. The status bar has to match the scene. A noon clock on a 2 AM argument gives it away.

articles.title: The Verification Airlock: A Different Approach to AI Agent Execution
articles.excerpt: How Headron combines deterministic verification, adaptive intelligence, and controlled execution. AI agents are becoming capable of working across entire software projects. They can inspect repositori…
articles.body: How Headron combines deterministic verification, adaptive intelligence, and controlled execution. AI agents are becoming capable of working across entire software projects. They can inspect repositories, modify files, run commands, and coordinate complex tasks. The difficult part is no longer getting an agent to act. It's determining which actions should be allowed, what evidence they require, and whether the results can be trusted. This is where Headron takes a different approach. The Deterministic Verification Airlock An AI agent can explain why its code should work. That explanation isn't verification. Headron separates the agent's proposed work from the system responsible for evaluating it. The verification airlock is the boundary between an agent's actions and an accepted result.
articles.author: Headeron

articles.title: Citation Tracing for Real-Estate Listing Discovery — A Staged Retrieval Architecture
articles.excerpt: Short answer: use staged retrieval with explicit collections, bounded queries, and source context that can be traced back to the exact listing PDF revision. That answer is intentionally less exciting…
articles.body: Short answer: use staged retrieval with explicit collections, bounded queries, and source context that can be traced back to the exact listing PDF revision. That answer is intentionally less exciting than choosing a vector index. It is more useful. In a fintech-adjacent property workflow, a user may ask, “Which listings allow a 30-day close?” The response needs evidence, not just a similarity score. Define the retrieval contract first, then price the lifecycle of that contract at scale. The field guide: choose a boundary before a database The clean boundary is: ingestion owns document identity; retrieval owns candidate selection; the answer layer owns citation rendering. Keep those responsibilities visible in logs and metrics.
articles.author: XanderCross2748

articles.title: What a preprint is — and what it isn't
articles.excerpt: A link appears in a group chat or a news story: researchers have posted a new study on arXiv, bioRxiv, or medRxiv. The PDF looks like a paper. It has a title, a methods section, figures, and a date. I…
articles.body: A link appears in a group chat or a news story: researchers have posted a new study on arXiv, bioRxiv, or medRxiv. The PDF looks like a paper. It has a title, a methods section, figures, and a date. It may already be written up as if the finding were established. For a reader who is not inside the field, the most useful first question is not "Is this true?" It is "What kind of document is this?" The core idea is simple: a preprint is a manuscript that the authors have posted publicly before formal peer review. The posting makes the work citable and time-stamped. It does not, by itself, certify that the results have been checked and endorsed by independent reviewers. That practice is older than the current platforms, but the modern, centralized version has a clear starting point.

articles.title: Why your Airbnb and Booking.com calendars are hours apart: iCal is polling, not push
articles.excerpt: A guest books a villa on Booking.com at 10:05. The host gets the confirmation email and assumes Airbnb now shows those nights as taken. It doesn't. Not yet. Until Airbnb next reads the Booking.com cal…
articles.body: A guest books a villa on Booking.com at 10:05. The host gets the confirmation email and assumes Airbnb now shows those nights as taken. It doesn't. Not yet. Until Airbnb next reads the Booking.com calendar link, the same nights are still open to anyone searching Airbnb. Underneath, this is a plain pull vs push problem, with a very physical failure mode: two guests, one room. This post looks at why calendar sync over iCal is always late, how long the gap is according to the platforms themselves, and why only a direct (push) connection really shrinks it. The sync schedules below come from the official help pages of Airbnb, Booking.com and Agoda, checked on 16 October 2026.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 10, 2013: Europe's GOCE satellite, the 'Ferrari of space,' fell out of orbit after mapping Earth's gravity field
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. GOCE, its name was short for Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer, launched in 2009 on a mission to map Earth's gravity like never before. But despite that successful mission, it was doomed in 2013 when it ran out of fuel . At the time, controllers weren't sure where GOCE would fall back to Earth . Some people worried that it might crash into a populated area. However, the small spacecraft broke up in the atmosphere and didn't cause any property damage. It disintegrated about 50 miles above the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. The European Space Agency called the mission a success. GOCE lasted far longer than expected.

articles.title: Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
articles.excerpt: Researcher finds 35,000 Grok Build apps wide open to anyone who looked for them.
articles.body: Grok Build, the vibe-coding agent from SpaceXSI, is leaking data—some of it proprietary business information and other sensitive secrets—from thousands of its users, including the very same Elon Musk-owned company that offers the platform, new research shows. The information is revealed through links allowing Grok Build users to share their apps with others. Grok takes steps to randomize the URLs so only people who know the exact URL can access the data stored there. A design decision by developers of the platform, however, completely torpedoes that objective and makes it possible for anyone to enumerate thousands of live Grok Build projects. Except in rare cases, clicking those links opens the app and reveals all data associated with it.

articles.title: A distant exoplanet mysteriously vanished from sight. Astronomers just discovered why
articles.excerpt: Astronomers have solved the mystery of an exoplanet that "disappeared" after seven years of observations.
articles.body: Astronomers have solved the mystery of an extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, that "disappeared" after seven years of observations. New research suggests that the planet hasn't vanished at all, but has been dragged off its orbit by an unseen planet. The exoplanet , designated TOI-2535 b, is located around 1,000 light-years away. TOI-2535 b was routinely observed with NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite ( TESS ) space telescope for seven years between April 2019 and March 2026 as it completed its 8.25-Earth day orbit of its parent star. That's 10 times quicker than the orbit of Mercury around the sun and means this blisteringly hot planet is classed as a " hot Jupiter ." However, something strange happened started to happen as astronomers observed the distant world.
